Claim: TQ exposure was associated with a strong reduction in Muv occurrence across the tested concentrations.
The primary Muv prevalence decreased from 90.5% to 61.2% to 23.5% across 0, 50 and 100 uM.
Pairwise treatment-associated differences remain robust under exact/Fisher inference and permutation testing.
The whole-animal pseudovulva distribution differs substantially across exposure groups.
Among Muv-positive animals, conditional pseudovulva count did not differ detectably across exposure groups.
The experiment provides phenotypic evidence from a Ras/MAPK-associated C. elegans model.
Progressive severity suppression among Muv-positive animals.
Biological replication based solely on N=343.
